question: What are the ids, first and last names of the customers who have ordered more than twice and have bought at least 3 items?
schema:
tenant=spider_e_commerce
tables:
  - Customer_Payment_Methods
      customer_id: int — customer id
      payment_method_code: str — payment method code values: 'Cheque', 'Credit Card', 'Direct Debit'
  - Customers
      customer_id: int — customer id
      gender_code: str — gender code values: 'Female', 'Male', 'Unknown'
      customer_first_name: str — customer first name
      customer_middle_initial: str — customer middle initial
      customer_last_name: str — customer last name
      email_address: str — email address
      login_name: str — login name
      login_password: str — login password
      phone_number: str — phone number
      address_line_1: str — address line 1
      town_city: str — town city
      county: str
      country: str values: 'USA'
  - Invoices
      invoice_number: int — invoice number
      invoice_status_code: str — invoice status code values: 'Issued', 'Paid'
      invoice_date: str — invoice date
  - Order_Items
      order_item_id: int — order item id
      product_id: int — product id
      order_id: int — order id
      order_item_status_code: str — order item status code values: 'Delivered', 'Out of Stock'
  - Orders
      order_id: int — order id
      customer_id: int — customer id
      order_status_code: str — order status code values: 'Cancelled', 'Delivered', 'Part Completed'
      date_order_placed: str — date order placed
  - Products
      product_id: int — product id
      parent_product_id: int — parent product id
      product_name: str — product name
      product_price: float — product price
      product_color: str — product color values: 'Red', 'Yellow'
      product_size: str — product size values: 'Medium', 'Small'
      product_description: str — product description
  - Shipment_Items
      shipment_id: int — shipment id
      order_item_id: int — order item id
  - Shipments
      shipment_id: int — shipment id
      order_id: int — order id
      invoice_number: int — invoice number
      shipment_tracking_number: str — shipment tracking number
      shipment_date: str — shipment date
relationships (many rows on the left per row on the right; join either way, chain through tables):
  - Customer_Payment_Methods.customer_id → Customers.customer_id
  - Orders.customer_id → Customers.customer_id
  - Order_Items.order_id → Orders.order_id
  - Order_Items.product_id → Products.product_id
  - Shipments.order_id → Orders.order_id
  - Shipments.invoice_number → Invoices.invoice_number
  - Shipment_Items.order_item_id → Order_Items.order_item_id
  - Shipment_Items.shipment_id → Shipments.shipment_id
gold_sql: SELECT T1.customer_id, ANY_VALUE(T1.customer_first_name), ANY_VALUE(T1.customer_last_name) FROM Customers AS T1 JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 INTERSECT SELECT T1.customer_id, ANY_VALUE(T1.customer_first_name), ANY_VALUE(T1.customer_last_name) FROM Customers AS T1 JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id JOIN Order_items AS T3 ON T2.order_id = T3.order_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
system_sql: SELECT `c`.`customer_id` AS `customer_id`, `c`.`customer_first_name` AS `customer_first_name`, `c`.`customer_last_name` AS `customer_last_name`, COUNT(DISTINCT `o`.`order_id`) AS `count_order_id`, COUNT(`oi`.`order_item_id`) AS `count_order_item_id` FROM `Customers` AS `c` JOIN `Orders` AS `o` ON `c`.`customer_id` = `o`.`customer_id` JOIN `Order_Items` AS `oi` ON `o`.`order_id` = `oi`.`order_id` GROUP BY `c`.`customer_id`, `c`.`customer_first_name`, `c`.`customer_last_name` HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT `o`.`order_id`) > 2 AND COUNT(`oi`.`order_item_id`) >= 3 LIMIT 10000
